simple: Free models from the Creator Store (the Toolbox) can hide bad scripts called backdoors. A backdoor lets the person who made it secretly control your game, steal data, or ruin it for players. Even a normal-looking car or house can have one. This page shows how to box in a model's scripts so they can only do what they really need.
analogy: Grabbing a free model is like taking a free toy from a stranger. Most are fine, but one might have a hidden microphone inside, so you check it and keep it in a room where it cannot hear much.
keyPoints: A backdoor is a hidden script that gives its creator secret server control of your game.
Backdoors often hide inside normal-looking models and may only switch on when a certain player joins or a command is typed.
The Toolbox shows when a model contains scripts, before and while you insert it.
Roblox moderation removes many bad models, but not all of them.
Best defense: sandbox it. Set Workspace's `SandboxedInstanceMode` to `Experimental`, set the model's `Sandboxed` property to true, then pick only the `Capabilities` it needs.
Be extra careful about giving a free model Network, DataStore, AssetRequire, CapabilityControl, or LoadString powers.
Read a model's scripts before using it. Watch for scrambled code or code pushed far off to the side with lots of spaces.
Popular, well-rated models are usually safer, but popularity does not guarantee safety.

terms.third-party asset: Something made by someone other than you, like a model from the Creator Store.
terms.Creator Store / Toolbox: The place in Studio where you can grab free models, images, sounds, and more made by others.
terms.backdoor: A sneaky script that lets its creator control your game without your permission.
terms.malicious: Made on purpose to cause harm.
terms.sandboxing: Putting something in a closed box with limited powers so it cannot affect the rest of your game.
terms.capability: One permission you can give a sandboxed model, like Audio or Physics.
terms.obfuscated: Made deliberately hard to read, often to hide what code really does.
terms.whitespace: Blank spaces and empty lines. Bad scripts can use lots of spaces to push code off the edge of the screen.

watchOut: Inserting a model without checking for scripts. Look for script icons and read every script inside.
Trusting a model just because it is popular. Still check it.
Giving a free model the Network or DataStore capability without knowing exactly why it needs it.
Missing hidden code. Scroll all the way right in long lines and be suspicious of unreadable code.
Panicking at "lacking Capability Unassigned" errors. During the beta some features do not work while sandboxed yet.
